answer: The sparrow test I would run is Signed supermarket loyalty tenure with grocer attestation: a loyalty account the grocer tracked across years of shops, so each new name must bring its own proof instead of reusing a sibling's. The verifier never sees the raw secret, only a proof that a loyalty account the grocer tracked across years of shops — so privacy survives, and the grove is that a stolen database buys the attacker nothing at all. A farm could afford one proof, maybe ten, but the ledge of a hundred is measured in weeks of work and thousands in fees, against a reward that shrinks per head.
